text:
alex: hit an OOM on prod node a100-04 serving a very long convo (~120k tokens). stack: alloc failed -> \"KV slab pinned\" repeated, then hard OOM. Not a typical fragmentation trace. cc @maria @sai

maria: rough. any recent kernel-selection changes or batching heuristics rolled in? sounds like reuse path didn't free prefixes.

sai: saw a similar symptom in canary but it was intermittent. quick sanity: is the kernel switcher toggling to a different kernel mid-request? that can leave KV refs sticky.

alex: logs show kernel switch around 2026-03-17T14:02:10Z then immediate growth of kv_bytes in metrics. snippet:```[INFO] kernel-switch: from=int8-fast to=qkv-fast seq_len=8192 request_id=xyz
[WARN] kv_alloc: slab=0x7f2c pinned=true refcount=3 request_id=xyz
[ERROR] alloc_failed: wanted=48MB avail=2MB pid=9876
```

maria: ok that's useful. can you grab a short heap profile and the kv slab map? `curl http://a100-04:6060/debug/heap` and `rdctl kv slab-map --host a100-04`

alex: pasted results in gist: https://gists.example/kv-heap-wobble, immediate observations: several medium slabs (32MB) marked non-evictable and refcount 3 for >2 minutes, while new allocations spike.

sai: likely cause: kernel-selection fastpath didn't set `evict_hint=false` correctly when switching back, so reuse path thinks slab is pinned. Also batching heuristic bumped to 128 streams which caused simultaneous allocations. two bad interactions.

samir: adding to investigation. quick mitigations to avoid further incidents: 1) reduce `serving.max_concurrent_streams` from 128 -> 64 2) enable `kv.soft_evict=true` to allow reclaim of lightly-referenced slabs 3) short-term: add a guarded fallback to model-variant `redwood-small-q4` on OOM so requests succeed albeit slower. anyone object?

maria: sounds good. can we instead set `kv.drain_ms=300` (was 2000) so we proactively drain KV reuse on kernel switch? that would reduce pinned window.

samir: +1 for drain_ms change. combine with soft_evict and stream cap. I'll prepare a patch to kernel-switcher to ensure `mark_evictable()` before toggling kernels.

ops-oncall: flagged hosts a100-04, a100-05 for immediate conservative config. will throttle ingress for affected clusters.

deploy-bot: rolling config change: cluster=prod-inference, patch_id=cfg-2026-03-17-01, params={"serving.max_concurrent_streams":"64","kv.soft_evict":"true","kv.drain_ms":"300"} scheduled in 5m.

alex: after applying config we saw reduced pressure. one request still hit a soft OOM but retried successfully with fallback. logs:```[WARN] kv_soft_evict: reclaimed=24MB freed_slabs=1 request_id=abc123
[INFO] fallback: model=redwood-small-q4 used after oom; latency+120ms request_id=abc123
```

maria: good sign. follow-ups: - samir to land kernel-switcher patch (add mark_evictable + unit tests) - infra to add a metric for "pinned_slab_count" and an alert threshold - devex to update best-practices doc about kernel switches and long-context serving - add canary with long-context heater (simulate 100k token dialog)

samir: patch ready, pushing in 30m. quick diff note: ensure transition does not flip `evictable` during active reuse window, use CAS on refcount. also add telemetry event `kernel_switch_evict_hint` so we can correlate in future.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-4421 "pinned-slab metric + alert" and dashboard panel.

maria: adding to postmortem draft. root cause: kernel-selection + aggressive batching -> KV reuse not drained -> pinned slabs accumulate -> memory cliff. mitigation: config roll, kernel-switcher patch, metric+alert, fallback model.

alex: thanks everyone. will keep thread updated if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
